definition.def: Your capacity for something is your ability to do it, or the amount of it that you are able to do.
examples: Our capacity for giving care, love and attention is limited. [+ for]
Her mental capacity and temperament are as remarkable as his.

definition.def: The capacity of something such as a factory, industry, or region is the quantity of things that it can produce or deliver with the equipment or resources that are available.
examples: ...the amount of spare capacity in the economy.
Bread factories are working at full capacity.
The region is valued for its coal and vast electricity-generating capacity.

definition.def: The capacity of a piece of equipment is its size or power, often measured in particular units.
examples: ...an aircraft with a bomb-carrying capacity of 454 kg. [+ of]
...a feature which gave the vehicles a much greater fuel capacity than other trucks.

definition.def: The capacity of a container is its volume, or the amount of liquid it can hold, measured in units such as litres or gallons.
examples: ...the fuel tanks, which had a capacity of 140 litres. [+ of]
Grease 6 ramekin dishes of 150 ml (5-6 fl oz) capacity.

definition.def: The capacity of a building, place, or vehicle is the number of people or things that it can hold. If a place is filled to capacity, it is as full as it can possibly be.
examples: Each stadium had a seating capacity of about 50,000. [+ of]
Toronto hospital maternity wards were filled to capacity.

definition.def: A capacity crowd or audience completely fills a theatre, sports stadium, or other place.
examples: A capacity crowd of 76,000 people was at Wembley football stadium for the event.

definition.def: If you do something in a particular capacity, you do it as part of a particular job or duty, or because you are representing a particular organization or person. [written]
examples: She visited the Philippines in her capacity as a Special Representative of Unicef. [+ as]
This article is written in a personal capacity.
Morley served in many capacities: as a critic, director, notable biographer and broadcaster.
